title: Unit – 3 : Session – 5 | Comprehensive Human Goal and Dimensions of Society
sections: Q1. The COMPREHENSIVE HUMAN GOAL has four parts: (1) RIGHT UNDERSTANDING and RIGHT FEELING (happiness) in every human being / in every Self; (2) PROSPERITY in every FAMILY; (3) FEARLESSNESS (trust) in SOCIETY; (4) CO-EXISTENCE (mutual fulfilment) in NATURE/EXISTENCE. These four are indivisible — individual happiness without family prosperity is hollow; prosperity without fearlessness in society is insecure; and all three are impossible without co-existence with the nature that supports us. Right understanding in the Self is the base from which the other three unfold.

Q2. The FIVE dimensions (systems) of human society that together realise the human goal are: (1) EDUCATION-SANSKAR — education to develop right understanding and right feeling, and sanskar (commitment/preparation) to live it; (2) HEALTH-SELF-REGULATION — health of the body and self-discipline in lifestyle; (3) PRODUCTION-WORK — producing physical facility in mutual enrichment with nature; (4) JUSTICE-PRESERVATION — justice (relationship with human beings) and preservation (relationship with rest of nature); (5) EXCHANGE-STORAGE — exchange of physical facility for mutual fulfilment and storage for mutual prosperity. All five operate at every level — family to world family.

Q3. The AVARTANSHEEL (cyclical) process is nature's own model: production that enriches while it produces — where the output of one process is the input of another, and nothing becomes waste (e.g., a tree takes CO2, gives oxygen, fruits and leaf-litter that feeds the soil, and the soil feeds the tree). Modern linear production (extract → produce → consume → dump) is non-cyclical: it DEPLETES resources at one end and POLLUTES at the other, because it takes from nature without returning anything nature can use. The remedy is to redesign production on the avartansheel pattern — cyclic, self-sustaining, mutually enriching.

Q4. Development by RELATIONSHIP means participating in nature's own cyclical, mutually fulfilling order — taking from nature what is needed for right utilisation while protecting and enriching it (like a farmer who nourishes the soil). Development by DOMINATION means treating nature as a mere stock to be conquered — maximum extraction, maximum consumption, minimum regard. The first gives continuity (resources regenerate, harmony sustains); the second gives short-term comfort and long-term crisis (depletion, pollution, climate change). The difference lies in the human being's assumption: nature as family versus nature as property.
